subject: Bridging handshake: evaluation checkpoints, infra handoff, keys & peering
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging handshake: evaluation checkpoints, infra handoff, keys & peering

Hi Sana —

Following our call this morning, attached is a concise mutual-action checklist to get the PO C environment into a production-like state for your eval. I pulled the items we agreed on into discrete owners and a tight cadence so we can close within the next 2 weeks if all parties move on schedule. Key asks below:

- Org & tenant bootstrap: create an Orbis test org and invite the Redwood eval service account (redwood-eval@orbis-org). Owner: Orbis onboarding. Target: 3/11.
- API keys & ephemeral flow: we will issue ephemeral API keys for the evaluation; sample flow attached. Owner: Redwood (Karthik). Target: 3/10 for sample, 3/12 for production test keys.
- IP allowlist: please confirm the static egress ranges you will allow (we listed required ranges in the attached doc). Owner: Orbis infra. Target: 3/11.
- VPC peering / private link: if you want VPC peering we need account IDs, peering contacts, and an initial test CIDR. Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) + Orbis infra. Target: peer established by 3/15 (if agreed).
- Canary test & acceptance: 48-hour canary with token-limited traffic, health checks and a rollback window. Owner: Orbis + Redwood. Proposed window: 3/16-3/18.

Attachments: MAP-commitments-v0.3.pdf (mutual action items, owners, and gating criteria).

Next steps: please reply with the single line confirmations for org invite, IP ranges, and peering interest. I will follow up with a short calendar block for a peering coordination call (30 min) if you want us to drive that.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks, this is very clear. Quick answers from our side:

- Org invite: yes, please invite redwood-eval@orbis-org to a new "orbis-eval" org; we will grant tester role.
- IP allowlist: we can open these ranges from our perimeter firewall — will confirm exact prefixes by EOD 3/10.
- Peering: we prefer to start with peering but may fall back to NAT + allowlist during the first week. Please share the peering checklist and the account ID format we need to provide.

Also can you confirm whether the ephemeral keys will rotate hourly or daily for the canary? That will affect our automation.

Sana Patel
Director, Cloud Platform
Orbis Health

Sana —

Great — quick clarifications inline:

- Org invite: will send invite today; we will use the eval service account redwood-eval@orbis-org (please confirm when accepted).
- Ephemeral keys: default plan is hourly rotation during the canary (short TTL to limit blast radius). If you prefer daily rotation we can accommodate; note that hourly requires a short client refresh flow (sample attached: ephemeral-key-sample.txt).
- Peering checklist & account IDs: Ben will own the peering orchestration. Ben — can you share the minimal info we need from Orbis (account ID, VPC name, preferred test CIDR) and whether you want to drive the cross-cloud peering template?

Proposed timeline (compressed):
- 3/10: Redwood sends sample ephemeral flow + send org invite
- 3/11: Orbis confirms IP prefixes and accepts org invite
- 3/12: Redwood issues test ephemeral keys; basic validation run
- 3/15: VPC peering established (if chosen)
- 3/16-3/18: Canary window

I attached the ephemeral key sample for your engineers.

Karthik
